text:
rachel: Heads up - ACME CSM pinged with a formal request for a 'bulk embeddings slab' offering: sustained 100k embeddings/hr, EU egress only, plus short bursts up to 15k per request during re-index windows. They want it as an opt-in to Starter and Scale. :eyes:

jon: got the profile? batch or steady?

rachel: @jon attached sample: mostly nightly batch windows (1-4h) and occasional day-time reindex spikes. They need deterministic throughput for downstream ML pipelines.

kevin: quick infra read: a sustained 100k/hr is achievable with reserved Dedicated capacity + aggressive batching. EU-only egress means isolate routing + KMS regional keys. Burst up to 15k reqs needs burst pool or token bucket.

sarah: product framing: we can do a slab (monthly commit in embeddings units with SLA) or a token-burst addon (pay-for-burst). Slab is simpler for legal/SLA; tokens give flexibility but complicate UX.

emma-sales: Sales input - customer prefers simple contract language and clear SLA number. They will only pay for committed throughput if we can guarantee it.

jon: implementation asks: meter per-second throughput, per-route reservation API, console toggle for EU egress, billing SKU that shows commit vs overage. Any timeline guesses?

kevin: rough: infra routing + KMS config ~2w, metering pipeline + billing events ~1w, console UI + API ~1w, end-to-end ~4w total if we don't reprioritize. Add 1-2w for testing and legal signoff.

rachel: launch checklist draft:
- SLA draft (throughput, availability, penalty/credit terms)
- Billing SKU and monthly reconciliation process
- Console purchase flow with EU egress toggle and visibility into committed units
- Pilot playbook with rate-limited rollout (1 customer -> closed beta)
- Security & privacy review for EU-only data egress

billing-bot: flag - need billing integration ticket and e2e test to validate commit vs overage invoicing.

jon: ops risk - if we expose per-route reservations, we need circuit breakers, autoscale guardrails, and fallback model variants to avoid cross-tenant impact.

kevin: infra-bot: recommend implementing a burst token pool that draws from reserved capacity but can be throttled by policy. Canary in EU region first.

sarah: product decision needed: which tiers get access? Starter + Scale makes sense from sales ask but operationally we should limit initial availability to Scale + pilot. Starter can be a later opt-in.

emma-sales: propose pilot economics: 3-month paid pilot at 70% list with a commitment floor. If they convert, credit pilot towards annual commitment.

rachel: negotiation approach aligns. I'll draft pilot contract language and a short SLA appendix.

jon: also add metrics to track during pilot: queue length, tail latency, batch efficiency, overage events, cost per 100k embeddings.

kevin: will build a cost model and expected utilization curves; we need to surface per-100k/hr incremental cost to finance.

rachel: action items:
- rachel -> pilot contract + SLA appendix by Thu EOD
- kevin -> infra checklist + cost model by Tue
- sarah -> product spec + console mock by Tue
- jon -> runbook for failure modes and autoscale knobs by Wed
- emma -> align Sales & CSM and create pilot intake doc by Wed
- billing-bot -> open billing integration ticket and test plan

kevin: one more thought - price burst tokens at a premium and include a soft cap to discourage uncontrolled bursts.

rachel: agreed. we'll iterate on pricing after cost model. i'll post the SLA draft here when ready. :white_check_mark:
